But mass spec also shows isotopic pattern: small peaks at +1, +2 etc typical for chlorine? The intensities: m/z 184.048 (intensity 10.25) relative to 183.045 (100). That's about 10% for M+1. That could be due to natural isotopic distribution of 13C (about 1.1% per carbon). For 10 carbons, expected M+1 ~11% which matches. So likely no halogen. Good.

Thus neutral formula C10H16NO2 (DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1 =10 -8 +0.5+1=3.5? Wait H/2 =8, N/2=0.5, so DBE=10-8+0.5+1=3.5 not integer, impossible. So formula must give integer DBE. So C10H16NO2 gives DBE = (2C+2+N-H-X)/2 = (20+2+1-16)/2 = (7)/2 =3.5 not allowed. So not correct.

Thus maybe neutral formula C10H14NO2? DBE = (20+2+1-14)/2 = (9)/2=4.5 not integer.

C10H12NO2? DBE = (20+2+1-12)/2 = (11)/2=5.5.

Thus need even H count to get integer DBE when N odd? Actually formula DBE = C - H/2 + N/2 +1. For integer DBE, (H + N) must be even. For C10, N=1, H must be odd to make H+N even. So H odd. So neutral H odd. Our candidate C10H15NO2 (H odd) gives DBE =10 -7.5 +0.5 +1 =4. So integer. Mass 181.1103 low.

C10H13NO2 (H odd) DBE =10 -6.5 +0.5 +1 =5. So integer. Mass 179.0946 low.

C10H17NO2 (H odd) DBE =10 -8.5 +0.5 +1 =3. So integer. Mass 183.1259 high.
